transcript.text:
Hi everyone! I'm really excited we're planning to use my late grandfather's 35mm camera for a family portrait session. I've got two unopened rolls of film ready to go, plus an external flash and a handheld light meter since the camera doesn't have a built-in flash.

Before we confirm any details, I'd like to go around the group as I usually do — I want to hear from everyone about timing, access, and any practical concerns. We're looking at either a Saturday or Sunday in mid-May 2027, and we can do the session either in my living room or out in the nearby park.

So let's start: what works best for everyone schedule-wise, and does anyone have a preference between the indoor and outdoor locations? Any concerns about lighting, weather, or anything else we should factor in?

transcript.text: Okay, here's what I wanted to share — I actually took Grandpa's camera to Rosa at the film shop last week to have it looked at. She inspected it and had some specific recommendations. First, she said we should use the ISO 200 black-and-white film for this session. Second, she found that the camera's internal light meter is unreliable, so she recommended we meter every single shot with the handheld light meter instead of relying on the camera's meter. And third — and this is especially relevant given Jordan's migraine concern — she recommended using Maya's living room rather than the park, because the indoor available light is steadier and more consistent. So between Jordan needing a no-flash session and Rosa's advice about steadier light indoors, it sounds like the living room would be the better call.
